text:
selene: Quick RFC follow-up — we need to pick a default pattern for private VPC egress. Comparing a per-tenant "siloed" overlay (each tenant gets its own regional egress pool/proxies) vs a shared regional relay (single relay per region with tenant tagging). Looking for concrete tradeoffs: cost, IP usage, failover, cert surface, and operations burden.

minh: leaning toward tenant-silo for compliance and data-path separation. Easier to prove isolation to auditors. :lock:

amos: shared relay wins on cost and IP efficiency. One pool per region is much easier to scale and maintain. But we lose per-tenant srcip preservation without extra plumbing.

jordyn: ops question — siloed implies per-tenant certs or mTLS + SNI routing. That's a nontrivial cert rotation + issuance surface. Also increases control plane state.

selene: wrote a tiny sketch of routing intent for the two options:
```yaml
# tenant-silo: each tenant maps to a dedicated egress pool
egress_pools:
  region-us-west-2:
    tenant-a: pool-az1, pool-az2
    tenant-b: pool-az1
# shared-relay: single regional pool with tenant tag enforcement
shared_relays:
  region-us-west-2: relay-01 (tags: tenant_id)
```

minh: failover note — siloed isolates blast radius per tenant, but you lose the ability to rehome cold capacity across tenants in an outage (we can't steal tenant-B IPs for tenant-A). That can be expensive for utilization.

networking_bot: RFC CI: rfc/2026/private-egress-overlay — tests passed (ci#314) :white_check_mark:

amos: quick cost back-of-envelope: shared-relay ~20-30% fewer IPs and ~25% less ops toil (one scaling pipeline). Siloed gives easier billing separation. Numbers vary with tenant churn.

jordyn: security pattern: shared-relay + per-tenant mTLS origination could preserve identity without per-tenant IPs, but we then need per-tenant cert issuance and rotation. Alternatively, tokenized routing at L7, but that impacts latency.

selene: Dedicated customers will ask for SLA-backed bandwidth & deterministic p99. Siloed makes quota enforcement simple (dedicated pools). Shared-relay requires careful QoS and isolation at scheduler level.

amos: proposal: hybrid default = shared regional relay (cheap, simple) + optional tenant-dedicated egress pools for enterprise/Dedicated customers. That gets us best of both worlds.

minh: hybrid seems pragmatic. Ops complexity jumps a bit (support both models) but it's manageable. We need to define the policy surface: how to request a dedicated pool, billing events, and cutover path.

jordyn: action item I care about: cert/identity doc for hybrid. I'll draft patterns: 1) per-tenant certs on dedicated pools, 2) mTLS with SNI + tokenized auth on shared relays, 3) short-lived client tokens for pathing.

selene: action items summary: 1) perf spike: p99 comparison shared vs siloed under mixed tenants (selene/minh) 2) IP consumption simulation (amos) 3) cert/rotation patterns doc (jordyn) 4) compliance checklist + pilot customers (minh). @amos @jordyn take point on 2 & 3?

amos: I'll run IP sim + utilization model, drop results in the RFC by EOD Friday.

jordyn: I'll spin up a doc with cert rotation patterns and rough latency impact for tokenized routing by Monday.

minh: I'll reach out to two pilot customers for compliance constraints and share any hard blockers.

selene: great — I'll update the RFC with hybrid recommendation draft and we can iterate. Thanks all :rocket:
